title: Vetala Extended Tale 95: The Ascetic and the Hungry Sparrow

full_text:
Under the flickering stars, Vikram captured the Vetala again. The ghost began:

"A holy ascetic lived on a mountain peak, subsisting on a single handful of parched rice every evening after twelve hours of meditation. One freezing evening, as he raised the handful to his mouth, a tiny shivering sparrow fell onto his lap, wings frozen and chest heaving with starvation.

The ascetic looked at the grains that sustained his own frail body, then looked at the dying bird. With a tender smile, he crushed the grains between his fingers, fed the sparrow crumb by crumb, and poured a drop of melted snow into its beak. The bird revived, chirped with joy, and took wing into the dawn. That night, the ascetic went hungry, yet felt an ecstasy of peace greater than years of solitary meditation.

Tell me, Vikram: did the ascetic break his ascetic discipline, or consummate it?"

King Vikramaditya replied: "He consummated his discipline in divine perfection. The goal of all austerity is to burn away the selfish ego and realize unity with all living beings. Giving his only food to a helpless bird was the supreme sacrificial offering."

"Infallible truth!" shouted the Vetala, and vanished into the branches.
moral: Surrendering one's own nourishment for a starving creature is the highest ritual sacrifice.
